summary: The Government of Canada advises exercising a high degree of caution for travel to Indonesia due to political and social tensions, terrorism threats, and violent crime throughout the country. Specific regions with higher warnings include all provinces of Indonesian Papua (except Raja Ampat Regency and Sorong city) due to violent incidents, militant threats, and kidnapping risks, as well as Aceh province and parts of East and West Kalimantan due to kidnapping threats.

rawLevel: Exercise a high degree of caution
summary: Thailand is under an overall advisory of 'Exercise a high degree of caution' due to ongoing political tensions, sporadic demonstrations, and an ongoing terrorism threat. Specific regions with higher warnings include the Thailand-Cambodia border (avoid all travel due to armed clashes and land mines) and the southern provinces of Narathiwat, Pattani, Yala, and southern Songkhla (avoid all travel due to violent separatist insurgent attacks). Political instability and military enforcement powers contribute to an unpredictable security environment.

summary: The Government of Canada advises exercising a high degree of caution in Türkiye due to the threat of terrorist attacks and possible demonstrations throughout the country. The advisory is higher in specific regions: avoid all travel within 10 km of the borders with Iraq and Syria due to terrorism and unpredictable security, and avoid non-essential travel to the southeastern provinces of Hakkari and Şırnak for the same reasons. Terrorism risks include armed attacks in major cities and potential targets such as transportation hubs and public areas.

summary: The Government of Canada advises exercising a high degree of caution for travel to Egypt due to ongoing tensions, an unpredictable security situation, and the threat of terrorism. Specific regions with higher warnings include Northern Sinai (avoid all travel due to terrorist activity and military operations), the Western Desert and Libyan border area (avoid all travel due to smuggling, terrorist activities, and armed groups), and the northern part of South Sinai (avoid non-essential travel due to terrorism threats).

The Government of Canada advises avoiding all travel to Kuwait due to a volatile security situation in the region, including ongoing military activity and missile/drone attacks that have struck civilian infrastructure. There is also a persistent threat of terrorism targeting foreign military installations, places of worship, government buildings, and public areas frequented by foreigners. Additionally, petty crime and violent crime, particularly in the Jleeb Al-Shuyoukh area of Kuwait City, pose risks.

The Government of Canada advises Canadians to avoid non-essential travel to Israel due to the volatile security situation in the region. Specific areas with higher warnings include Jerusalem (avoid non-essential travel), the Golan Heights bordering Syria (avoid all travel), the area within 5 km of the Lebanon border (avoid all travel), and the area within 10 km of the Gaza Strip border (avoid all travel). The advisory cites ongoing military activity, rocket and mortar fire, and military operations as primary concerns.
